invalid_input_controls: EX1 fixture is not explicitly synthetic and public-development-only
risk confidence level is missing, non-finite or outside [0,1)
risk aversion lambda is missing, non-finite or outside [0,1)
pure CVaR lambda=1 is accepted despite missing strict-monotonicity condition
action-conditioned probabilities do not sum to one
negative/non-finite loss or non-positive probability in finite risk distribution
risk distribution probability mass does not sum to one
nested action has a positive-probability successor with no feasible continuation
static policy enumeration violates hard service floors
multiple policy actions are assigned to the same observable information state
hidden/future scenario identifier enters an observation history
transition observation differs from the successor's appended observation
resource conservation equation fails along a transition
duplicate canonical observable histories are treated as separate decisions
terminal outcome has non-null observation or non-terminal outcome omits its observation
static terminal-risk comparator and nested recursion use different alpha/lambda parameters
boundary_cases: lambda=0 reduces the one-period map to expectation
lambda approaches one from below but remains strictly monotone
one-point loss distribution has CVaR equal to its only loss
fractional upper-tail mass is handled by the Rockafellar-Uryasev formula
a different branch dominates terminal tail while a local gamble reverses under nested risk
all candidate policies violate a pathwise service floor and the report is explicitly infeasible/null
lambda=0 reduces the one-period map and nested recursion to expected cost
lambda just below one remains admissible and strictly monotone
alpha=0 reduces CVaR_0 to expectation under the upper-loss Rockafellar-Uryasev convention
alpha approaching one from below approaches the maximum support loss
round_trip_requirements: risk confidence alpha and lambda remain unchanged in evaluator output
same terminal cost distribution is used for static mean and CVaR
static objective equals (1-lambda)*terminal mean + lambda*terminal CVaR
nested objective uses the same one-period map at every observable information state
nested and static policies retain one action per canonical observable history
transition probabilities and successor observations remain attached to their incoming outcomes
risk units and total cost units remain identical
non_claims: No confirmatory or real-world outcome data
No claim that pure nested CVaR at lambda=1 provides strict monotonicity
No unconditional theorem claim beyond the assumptions of the cited dynamic-programming formulation
No SOTA superiority, operational deployment, readiness or certification claim
